scenes.say: Ever wonder what actually serves your .NET web apps on Windows? Let's break down IIS basics.

scenes.label: Sites
scenes.sub: Each site binds to an IP, port, and host header.
scenes.say: Each IIS site connects to a specific IP address, port, and host name. That's how it knows which traffic belongs where.

rows.b: Isolates each app in its own worker
Runs under its own service account

scenes.say: Every app runs in its own application pool, handled by a worker process. Each pool uses its own identity, which helps with security and stability.

scenes.title: IIS Management
scenes.say: You can list sites, check app pools, or restart a pool with these PowerShell commands. Super useful for troubleshooting.

scenes.question: App pool keeps stopping. What next?
scenes.right: Check the Application event log for real errors—rapid-fail protection means repeated crashes.
scenes.say: If your app pool keeps stopping, don't just restart it. Check the Application event log. IIS might be protecting you from repeated crashes.
